reliefAccounts.title: The Mercy Slip
reliefAccounts.first: You put Dot on the crew roll. Her berth belongs with the people who worked the crossing.
reliefAccounts.second: You issue Dot the missing passage slip. She keeps the bead threaded through its corner.
firstReplies: Dot has taken the early watch. She signs with the shipwright’s punch.
Dot ferried the sisters home. Ina found the blue bead where she had left it.
secondReplies: Dot's first fare slip hangs above the public till. Children ride free on watch nights.
Dot punched two return tickets, one for each sister, and slipped the bead into Ina’s hand.

reliefAccounts.title: Wickwater Fen
reliefAccounts.first: You hang the lamp tender’s name inside the hood. Boats can thank Oli by name.
reliefAccounts.second: The orchard families go down as the keepers of the spring. Oli leaves a full jar on their wall.
firstReplies: Oli hangs a little green light outside every watch hut.
Oli leaves a lamp between the sisters’ doors. Ina brings it in when Tavi gets home.
secondReplies: The orchard families bring their oil a jar at a time. The fen lights last the winter.
Ina took an empty jar to the orchard. She came back with oil, three apples and muddy knees.

reliefAccounts.title: The Linen Courts
reliefAccounts.first: The linen court is entered as a place of shelter. Its gate will stay open in bad weather.
reliefAccounts.second: The cloth code goes to the ferry crews. Three knots now mean an open door on either shore.
firstReplies: Eda has made the first bed by the watch door. The hem is folded once.
Eda found the two sisters asleep on the chalk-star cot, their muddy boots under the rail.
secondReplies: Every watch boat flies the three-knotted cloth. There is a dry place on either bank.
Tavi tied three knots in a clean cloth and hung it from the kitchen window.

reliefAccounts.title: Kite Crag
reliefAccounts.first: Ivo signs in his own hand. He was the pilot of the line even if he never stepped aboard.
reliefAccounts.second: Ivo gives each hand an inch of the old scarf. They write the crew names beneath its red edge.
firstReplies: Ivo teaches the new pilots to fly a line in a crosswind. He keeps the little kite for himself.
Ivo let Ina hold the line. When the kite rose, she laughed and wound it out another arm’s length.
secondReplies: Six strips of red scarf hang in the new watchroom. Each carries a different hand.
The landing crew passed the scarf to Ina. She stitched the strips together on the return boat.

reliefAccounts.title: Sounding Bay
reliefAccounts.first: Fenel enters the sounder’s name under the depth. Next winter’s pilots will know whom to ask.
reliefAccounts.second: The new channel is entered as public knowledge. Both landings receive copies of the soundings.
firstReplies: Fenel writes his name on the pilot board and leaves the lead line beneath it.
The sisters took the channel at slack water. At the second leather tongue, Fenel waved them through.
secondReplies: Both shores copied the soundings. The night pilots now argue over who gets the first clean chart.
Ina has added one small mark to the public chart, a dry stone where two people can sit.

reliefAccounts.title: The Supper Steps
reliefAccounts.first: Nan puts her floury hand against the bell book. It keeps the mark of the person who fed the watch.
reliefAccounts.second: Every seat is entered, even the one at the end for the stranger who steers home.
firstReplies: Nan takes the oven watch. A crescent on the first crust tells the crew she is there.
Nan kept two crescent loaves warm until Tavi and Ina came down the steps.
secondReplies: There is always a chair by the watchroom door. On the first night an unknown ferryman took it.
Ina sat in the last chair. Nan moved her own plate over and made room for Tavi.

roadLeaves.name: Mara · Orchard post
roadLeaves.shared: A graft takes when the two cuts grow one skin. Come evening nine children cut nine lanterns from my winter quinces. You should see them waiting their turns at the bell.
roadLeaves.freed: Ina came for a cutting. She held the knife backward until I showed her. We planted the graft by her door. By supper she had asked me three times when it might flower.

roadLeaves.name: Jori · Tileworks post
roadLeaves.shared: I made a thumb tile for each new keeper. Once their shift is done they lay it warm-side down on the sill. My daughter can tell who worked the night by touching the clay.
roadLeaves.freed: Tavi asked for a roof tile with no mark on it. She and Ina sat on my kiln step drawing sea birds into the wet clay with the same pin.

roadLeaves.name: Senn · Archive post
roadLeaves.shared: In the index I wrote room for ten hands, although only nine households live along the road. A stranger ought to be able to sign. You did.
roadLeaves.freed: The day the bell let her go, Ina brought the book back herself. She crossed out the word missing. She left the space after her name quite empty.

roadLeaves.name: Tern · Beacon post
roadLeaves.shared: Someone left a lamp in the cairn for whoever takes the hill after dark. Tonight it was my turn. I left dry socks for the next pair of feet.
roadLeaves.freed: My sister walked the high mile with Ina. Neither said much. At the last cairn they left two green stones in the dry niche, one for each return.

roadLeaves.name: Issa · Water court
roadLeaves.shared: The closure is lifted in nine different hands. My seal sits at the bottom with the rest. The right of way belongs to the next person who needs it.
roadLeaves.freed: Today a young bellmender asked me if she needed leave to use the road. I took the old closure plate down and gave it to her for a boat anchor.

theatreInvitation: TAVI / My sister and I made a paper theatre behind the market. I crossed her out of the play after the flood. Before I ask anything of you, I want you to see what happened. Take the blue courtyard door beside my stall.
theatreCredits: I kept the programme. ‘Ina, bellmender.’ People thought I made that bell on my own.
I kept the programme. ‘Ina, lock runner.’ Now when the children put on the play, somebody has to run.
dawnEntry: Ina’s kitchen song. Three knocks on our bedroom wall meant morning. Two cups on the table, one chair by the stove. One knock from the landing meant I made it home.
dawnVerses: Leaf, Tide, Leaf. Three knocks on our bedroom wall meant morning.
Ember, Ember, Tide. Two cups on the table, one chair by the stove.
Tide, Leaf, Ember. One knock from the landing meant I made it home.
dawnEnding: At first light Tavi winds the music box. Three knocks answer from every house on the hill.
At breakfast Ina drums three notes on the kitchen door. Tavi knows them before she turns.
woodEntry: Linn’s school linen. Ina put her thumb through the survey as a child. Linn darned it in red. The three instruments sing again, and her kitchen door is on the latch.
pressEntry: Ossa’s contact sheet. Pella crossed with the cradle. The water rose beyond the school ladder. Ina held the gate with her left hand.
pilotMail: Ash’s reed tube holds a charcoal drawing of Tavi. The short fringe and the little nick in her eyebrow are unmistakable. Ina drew it during the flood.
pilotEndings: Orla’s drawing has a place under the market bell. Tavi brushes the charcoal fringe with one finger. ‘I cut it myself that summer. She remembered.’
Tavi unrolls the drawing. Ina takes a burned twig from the stove and adds a second face beside the first. ‘There. Both of us.’
swallowEntries: Fen has written Ina’s name in full beside the night boat. Her four deliveries are on the lock wall.
Fen’s book bears a tiny swallow. Ina touches the mark and smiles. The lock crew knows whose it is.
parishLedger: Ada’s seal restores three addresses to the toll map: the Oar House, the school at Penny Reach, and the bell lock.
parishEndings: The new watch list gives every runner a meeting place. Against Ina’s name Ada has written Penny Reach school.
Ina traces the three names on Ada’s map. ‘Penny Reach. My peg was the third one from the door.’
supperEndings: Nell, Ara and Wen sign together for the first morning watch. Iona brings four bowls up to the tower.
Ina hears the pans from the harbour kitchen. ‘I remember that one.’ She takes a fourth bowl and calls for Tavi.

logEndings: Elin has signed for the night tide. Six lines stand open for volunteers.
Ina opens the pilots’ book to the last page. “Do you think Elin would teach me to steer?”
